title: Evaluation of the combined aftercare for addiction disorders with “coobi care”
summary: This study examines whether combined aftercare with digital support for people with addiction disorders is equivalent to conventional aftercare. Participants in the intervention group use the “coobi care” app and a smartwatch for six months and also attend 10 counseling sessions plus 2 appointments with support persons. In the control group, they receive the usual aftercare with 20 counseling sessions plus 2 appointments with support persons, without the app and smartwatch. The primary goal is to test whether the combined aftercare is used at least as often as the traditional aftercare (attendance at appointments). In addition, the study will examine whether it achieves equivalent results in terms of important outcomes such as relapses, personal confidence, mental well-being, and ability to work.

interventions.name: The intervention group receives "coobi care" digital support alongside a reduced schedule of 10+2 face-to-face aftercare sessions.
The control group follows the standard 20+2 session aftercare program without digital tools.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosed substance-related addiction disorder (F10-F16, F18, F19, except tobacco addiction), optionally with other substance addictions
- The ability and access to use a smartphone
- Adequate knowledge of German
- Willingness to participate in aftercare at one of the cooperating facilities.
Exclusion criteria:
- severe comorbidities with acute symptoms, e.g., acute schizophrenia or acute suicidality
- problematic media use
- significant learning difficulties that restrict the ability to participate
